## Stop: routeability heuristic drift

- STOP process:worker-routeability-drift | 2026-07-29 | After commit `ef0441040`, the batch worker began staging a partial batch dominated by non-HMI microbiome/infant NEC papers because the mechanical routeability heuristic was matching broad phrases such as "lead to" rather than confirmed heavy-metal evidence. I stopped the worker before this partial batch committed.
- ROLLBACK uncommitted-partial-batch | Removed 72 uncommitted source pages generated after `ef0441040` and restored generated evidence files to the committed state. No partial-batch source pages were committed.
- STATUS committed-through | `ef0441040` | 11 batches committed from `/Volumes/HMI-Library/heavy-metal-index-raw` (2,200 source pages total in this run).

## Correction: the 11 committed batches were contaminated too, and have been removed

The stop note above scoped the routeability drift to the uncommitted partial batch. That
scoping was wrong. The drift was structural in the worker's mechanical extractors, so it
was present in every one of the 11 committed batches, not only in the batch that was
caught. Measured across the 2,200 committed pages before removal:

| Defect | Measurement |
| --- | --- |
| `metals` asserts Al with no aluminium term anywhere in the extracted evidence | 2,116 of 2,184 pages (97%) |
| `metals` asserts Pb with no lead/Pb term in the extracted evidence | 856 of 1,598 pages (54%) |
| No spelled-out metal term at all in the extracted evidence | 1,459 of 2,200 pages (66%) |
| `cite_key` first token is the literal word `authors`, not a surname | 1,881 of 2,200 pages (86%) |
| `year: 2026` fallback asserted instead of the real publication year | 2,009 of 2,200 pages (91%) |
| Routing rows generated from junk cite-keys | 2,715 of 8,110 committed rows (33%) |

Root causes in `tmp/codex-bulk-ingest-worker-batch.mjs`:

- `detectMetals` matched bare two-letter symbols case-insensitively against lowercased
  full text. `/\bal\b/` matches "et al.", which appears in essentially every paper, so
  Al was asserted on 99.3% of pages. `/\bcd\b/`, `/\bni\b/`, `/\bcr\b/`, `/\bsn\b/` and
  `/\bhg\b/` fail the same way, and `/\blead\b/` matches the verb in "lead to".
- The no-evidence gate was `metals.length === 0 || nums.lines.length < 3`. Because
  `detectMetals` almost never returned empty, the gate never fired. Its numeric-line test
  also accepted the generic tokens `mean|median|range|Table|n =`, so any paper with a
  table passed regardless of subject matter.
- `detectProducts` matched `/cod/` unanchored, so "code", "coding" and "codebook" routed
  papers to `fish-marine-non-predatory`.
- `parseAuthors` returned "et al." as the author, and `firstSurname` reduced it to `al`
  or fell through to the literal `authors`, producing the junk cite-keys. `parseYear`
  defaulted to 2026 whenever no year was matched in the first 40 KB.

Topical drift also reached the committed batches: 184 pages came from
`essential_oils_antimicrobial_CLEAN`, plus Long COVID (78), female infertility (64),
candida (44), erectile dysfunction (42), cerebral palsy (41) and fibromyalgia (27)
folders. Metal-exposure health-outcome papers are in scope by default per
`docs/conventions`, so folder topic alone is not the defect; the defect is that these
pages asserted analyte scope the sources do not support.

Action taken: all 2,200 source pages from the 11 batch commits were removed and
`data/evidence/product_source_routing_audit.csv` was regenerated, dropping 8,110 rows to
4,605 with exit 0 and 0 blocking. No content is lost: every PDF remains in
`/Volumes/HMI-Library/heavy-metal-index-raw` and each removed page recorded its
`raw_path` and `raw_sha256`, so the corpus is fully re-ingestable once the extractors are
fixed. Direction of this edit per CLAUDE.md Part 2: toward the literature. It removes
analyte and provenance claims the sources do not support.

Note on the passing routing audit: `npm run evidence:source-routes` reported 0 blocking
throughout the run and that was accurate. The audit checks that frontmatter resolves to
known target pages, not that the frontmatter is true. A green routing audit is not
evidence that the ingest was sound, and should not be reported as though it were.

Residual, not addressed here: 126 source pages from earlier runs still carry junk
`authors*`/`al*` cite-keys. Most are genuine in-scope papers with real years and real
metal subject matter, so they need cite-key repair rather than removal. Nine
`authors2026-*` pages from the pre-batch serial run still hold routing rows and need
per-page review. `tools/lib/cite-key-validity.mjs`, the honest-minting gate from the
open PR #83, is absent from this tree, which is why 1,881 `authors2026-*` keys were
committable at all. Landing that gate is the structural fix.
